newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The UN Development Programme (UNDP) would expand activities in Bangladesh, said its resident representative David E Lockwood when he called on Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in Dhaka on Sunday.
Opposition leader and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia on Sunday demanded formation of a parliamentary probe body to find out the causes of the recent slide in stock prices.
The number of disabled is about 12 milllion in Bangladesh, according to an estimate of the World Health Organisation (WHO).
The Indian border security forces shot dead three Bangladeshi nationals on Friday at a border point in southwestern Kushtia district.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told a senior UN official on Sunday that her government would make the parliament the "centre of all activities".
British entrepreneurs are likely to fund the proposed development of the airport in the port city of Chittagong.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina leaves for USA on Wednesday night to attend the World Micro Credit summit beginning in Washington on February 2.

Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed left Dhaka on Sunday for Brussels to negotiate with European Union the future of Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) of the country's garments export.
